questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: After 'Hardly' use inversion with the past perfect: Hardly had I left.

wrongReasons.hardly i had left the office when it sta: After 'Hardly' at the start, the auxiliary 'had' must come before the subject: Hardly had I left.
wrongReasons.hardly had i left the office when it was: Keep the pattern 'Hardly had I left ... when it started to snow'. Only the word order of the first part needs to change.

questions.wrong: Hardly I had left the office when it started to snow.
solutions: Hardly had I left the office when it started to snow.

questions.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Rewrite it correctly.
questions.explanation: In an inverted third conditional, use 'Had + subject + past participle': Had I known.

wrongReasons.had i would known, i would have helped: In an inverted conditional, 'Had' replaces 'If' and is followed by the subject and a past participle. We do not add 'would': Had I known.
wrongReasons.if i had known, i would have helped: This sentence is correct in meaning, but the task is to use the inverted form 'Had I known'.

questions.wrong: Had I would known, I would have helped.
solutions: Had I known, I would have helped.
